SEPARATION AGREEMENT AND GENERAL RELEASE

November 14, 2025

Hector Bancroft
Naperville, Illinois

Re: Separation Agreement and General Release

Dear Mr. Bancroft:

This Separation Agreement and General Release (this "Agreement") is entered into as of November 14, 2025 (the "Effective Date"), by and between Meridian Mechanical of Illinois, LLC, an Illinois limited liability company with principal offices located at 1455 Busse Road, Elk Grove Village, Illinois 60007 ("Company"), and Hector Bancroft ("Employee").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Employee has been employed by Company as a Lead Installation Technician at the Company's Naperville branch; and

WHEREAS, due to a position elimination within the Company's operations, Company has determined to separate Employee from employment; and

WHEREAS, Company desires to provide Employee with severance consideration in exchange for Employee's execution of this Agreement, including a general release of claims against the Company and others; and

WHEREAS, Employee and Company desire to resolve all matters relating to Employee's employment and separation from employment on the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Employee and Company agree as follows:

1. SEPARATION DATE

Employee's employment with Company shall terminate effective as of the close of business on November 14, 2025 (the "Separation Date"). On the Separation Date, all of Employee's rights and obligations as an employee of Company shall cease, except as expressly provided in this Agreement or as required by law. Employee acknowledges that the termination of employment is due to a position elimination and is not a termination for cause. Employee shall return all Company property, including but not limited to tools, equipment, access badges, keys, documents, and any other property belonging to the Company on or before the Separation Date.

2. SEVERANCE

In consideration for Employee's execution of this Agreement without revocation and Employee's full compliance with all terms and conditions hereof, Company shall pay to Employee severance pay equal to six (6) weeks of Employee's regular wages, calculated at Employee's hourly rate in effect on the Separation Date. The total severance payment shall be Ten Thousand One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($10,150.00). This severance payment shall be paid to Employee in a single lump sum, less all applicable federal, state, and local taxes and withholdings, within fourteen (14) days following the expiration of the revocation period set forth in Section 5 below, provided that Employee has not revoked this Agreement in accordance with Section 5. The payment shall be made by check or direct deposit to Employee's account on file with the Company's payroll department.

3. GENERAL RELEASE AND WAIVER OF CLAIMS

3.1 Release by Employee. In consideration of the severance payment set forth in Section 2 and the other consideration provided herein, Employee hereby releases, acquits, and discharges the Company, its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the "Releasees") from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, liabilities, and obligations of any nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, arising out of or relating to Employee's employment with the Company, the termination of that employment, or Employee's claims against the Company or any Releasee, including but not limited to:

a) Any and all claims for compensation, wages, bonuses, incentive pay, or other remuneration;

b) Any and all claims arising under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Civil Rights Act of 1991, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967, the Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act of 2008, and any state or local equivalents;

c) Any and all claims arising under the Fair Labor Standards Act and corresponding state wage and hour laws, including claims for overtime compensation, minimum wage, or wage statement penalties;

d) Any and all claims arising under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 and related state law;

e) Any and all claims for breach of contract, wrongful termination, tort claims, or claims in equity;

f) Any and all claims for discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or any other employment-related claim;

g) Any and all claims for emotional distress, personal injury, property damage, or similar claims;

h) Any and all claims for attorneys' fees, costs, or other relief related to any claim described above; and

i) Any and all other claims, rights, and causes of action relating to Employee's employment or separation from employment, whether arising under federal, state, local, or common law, known or unknown.

3.2 Excluded Claims. Notwithstanding Section 3.1, this release does not include any claims or rights that cannot be waived by law, including but not limited to claims arising after the Effective Date of this Agreement, claims for unemployment insurance benefits, claims for workers' compensation benefits to the extent provided by law, claims for vested benefits under any Company-sponsored retirement or benefit plan (to the extent Employee has vested rights therein), or any statutory rights that are expressly not waivable under applicable law.

3.3 Scope of Release. Employee acknowledges that this release is intended to be a general release and is written in broad terms so as to effect a complete settlement of all disputes between Employee and the Company relating to Employee's employment and separation from employment. Employee acknowledges having read this release and understanding its broad scope and consequences.

4. CONTINUING OBLIGATIONS

4.1 Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation. Employee acknowledges and reaffirms that Employee remains bound by the Technician Employment Agreement dated June 7, 2021 (the "Employment Agreement"), including without limitation the covenants not to compete and not to solicit customers or employees of the Company contained therein. Employee agrees that Employee shall continue to comply fully with all terms and conditions of the Employment Agreement as modified or supplemented by this Agreement. Employee acknowledges that the restrictions contained in the Employment Agreement are reasonable in scope, duration, and geography and are necessary to protect the Company's legitimate business interests, including the Company's trade secrets and confidential business information.

4.2 Confidential Information. Employee acknowledges that during Employment, Employee had access to and became familiar with the Company's confidential information and trade secrets, including but not limited to customer lists, pricing information, business methods, service procedures, operational data, and other proprietary information. Employee agrees that Employee shall maintain the confidentiality of all such information, shall not disclose such information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Company, and shall not use such information for any purpose other than as necessary in the course of performing Employee's duties for the Company. These confidentiality obligations shall continue indefinitely and shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

4.3 Return of Property. Employee represents and warrants that Employee has returned or shall return, on or before the Separation Date, all Company property in Employee's possession or control, including but not limited to tools, diagnostic equipment, keys, access cards, documents, and any other tangible property belonging to the Company. Employee shall be responsible for any damage to or loss of Company property, except for ordinary wear and tear.

4.4 Cooperation. Employee agrees to cooperate with the Company in all matters relating to the transition of Employee's duties, including but not limited to making himself available to answer questions about ongoing projects, customer accounts, or administrative matters, for a reasonable period of time following the Separation Date, at times mutually convenient to the parties. Any such cooperation shall be provided at no additional cost to Employee beyond the severance payment provided herein.

5. REVIEW PERIOD AND REVOCATION RIGHTS

5.1 Review Period. Employee acknowledges that Employee is being provided with this Agreement for Employee's review and that Employee has been advised to consult with legal counsel regarding the terms and conditions hereof. Employee shall have twenty-one (21) calendar days from the date of this Agreement within which to review this Agreement before execution (the "Review Period"). The Company encourages Employee to review this Agreement with legal counsel and is willing to discuss the terms hereof with Employee during this Review Period. This 21-day Review Period may be waived by Employee in writing, in which case this Agreement may be executed at any time prior to the expiration of the 21-day period.

5.2 Revocation Rights. Employee shall have an additional seven (7) calendar days following the date of Employee's execution of this Agreement during which Employee may revoke this Agreement by providing written notice of revocation to the Company. Such written notice of revocation must be signed by Employee and delivered personally, by certified mail, or by email to the Company's Chief Operating Officer at the Company's principal address set forth above or to such other address as the Company may designate from time to time. Any revocation notice must be received by the Company no later than 5:00 p.m. Central Time on the seventh (7th) day following Employee's execution of this Agreement. If Employee timely revokes this Agreement, this Agreement shall become null and void, the Company shall have no obligation to pay the severance payment described in Section 2, and the parties shall return to their respective positions as of the date of this Agreement, except that the termination of employment shall remain effective.

5.3 Effectiveness. This Agreement shall become effective and binding upon Employee eight (8) calendar days following Employee's execution of this Agreement (the "Effective Date of this Agreement"), provided that Employee does not timely revoke this Agreement in accordance with Section 5.2. Following the Effective Date of this Agreement and expiration of the revocation period, neither Employee nor the Company shall have any further right to rescind or cancel this Agreement except as may be required by law.

6. SEVERANCE ACCOUNT; RELEASE OF LIABILITY

Employee acknowledges that the severance payment provided in Section 2 constitutes full and final settlement of any and all claims arising out of or relating to Employee's employment with the Company and Employee's separation from employment. This severance payment shall be paid from the Company's general operating funds and shall not affect Employee's eligibility for any unemployment insurance benefits that Employee may be entitled to claim under applicable law. Employee further acknowledges and agrees that, with the exception of the severance payment specified in Section 2 and any benefits to which Employee is entitled by law (such as COBRA continuation coverage or vested retirement benefits), Employee shall receive no other compensation, severance, or benefits from the Company.

7. CONTINUING BENEFITS

7.1 Health Insurance. Employee shall have the right to elect continuation of health insurance coverage under the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 (COBRA) if Employee is entitled to such continuation coverage. Any COBRA continuation coverage shall be at Employee's sole cost and expense. Information regarding COBRA continuation coverage shall be provided to Employee in accordance with applicable law.

7.2 Accrued Paid Time Off. Any accrued but unused paid time off (vacation, personal days, or sick leave) that Employee is entitled to under Illinois law and Company policy shall be paid to Employee at the Employee's regular hourly rate in effect on the Separation Date. Such payment shall be made in accordance with applicable law and shall be included in Employee's final paycheck, which shall be issued in accordance with applicable Illinois wage and hour laws.

7.3 Other Benefits. Upon the Separation Date, Employee shall cease to participate in any other employee benefit plans, programs, or arrangements maintained by the Company, except to the extent expressly required by law or the terms of any such plan.

8. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

8.1 Authority. Each party represents and warrants that it has full authority to enter into this Agreement and that the person executing this Agreement on its behalf has been duly authorized to do so.

8.2 Acknowledgments. Employee acknowledges and represents that:

a) Employee has read this Agreement carefully;

b) Employee understands the terms and conditions of this Agreement;

c) Employee is entering into this Agreement voluntarily and of Employee's own free will;

d) Employee has been advised by the Company to consult with legal counsel regarding this Agreement;

e) Employee understands that by executing this Agreement, Employee is waiving and releasing claims that Employee may have against the Company;

f) Employee has been given adequate time to review this Agreement and consult with legal counsel if Employee desires; and

g) Employee is not under any duress or undue influence in executing this Agreement.

8.3 No Admission. Neither the payment of severance nor the execution of this Agreement shall be construed or interpreted as an admission by the Company of any liability, wrongdoing, or breach of law, regulation, contract, or Employee's rights. The Company denies any and all allegations or claims of wrongdoing or liability and is providing the severance payment solely as a business decision and settlement of disputed claims.

9. NOTICE REGARDING RIGHTS UNDER THE AGE DISCRIMINATION IN EMPLOYMENT ACT

Employee acknowledges receipt of written notice regarding Employee's rights and obligations under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), 29 U.S.C. § 621 et seq., and the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (OWBPA), 29 U.S.C. § 626(f). In particular, Employee understands and acknowledges that:

a) Employee is waiving age discrimination claims and is entitled to receive the specific notice required by the OWBPA;

b) Employee has been advised to consult with an attorney before entering into this Agreement;

c) Employee has had at least twenty-one (21) calendar days to review this Agreement;

d) Employee will have seven (7) calendar days to revoke this Agreement after execution if Employee so chooses;

e) This Agreement and the severance payment constitute adequate consideration for the waiver of ADEA rights; and

f) The Company is providing Employee with information regarding the basis for Employee's separation from employment.

10. RESIGNATION; SEPARATION FROM EMPLOYMENT

10.1 Resignation. By signing this Agreement, Employee acknowledges and agrees that Employee's employment with the Company is being terminated on the Separation Date and that Employee is not resigning from employment. Employee shall not represent to any third party that Employee resigned from the Company.

10.2 Reference. Employee acknowledges that the Company may provide factual information regarding Employee's dates of employment, title, and compensation to prospective employers or other third parties. The Company shall not disclose information regarding the circumstances of Employee's separation, except as required by law or subpoena.

11. MUTUAL CONFIDENTIALITY

Employee and Company each agree to maintain the confidentiality of the terms and conditions of this Agreement, except that each may disclose the terms to the extent necessary to (a) comply with law or legal process, (b) enforce this Agreement, (c) report to the Company's accountants or tax advisors, (d) disclose to immediate family members or personal legal counsel, or (e) report to government agencies as required by law.

12. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

12.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with the Employment Agreement referenced herein, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, agreements, and understandings, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter of this Agreement.

12.2 Amendment. This Agreement may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written document signed by Employee and an authorized representative of the Company.

12.3 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect to the maximum extent permitted by law, and the invalid provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable.

12.4 Waiver. The failure of either party to enforce any provision of this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of that provision or any other provision hereof.

12.5 Successors and Assigns. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and assigns. Employee's rights and obligations hereunder may not be assigned.

12.6 Construction. This Agreement shall be construed according to its terms and shall not be construed more strictly against either party.

12.7 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

12.8 Notices. Any notice, demand, or request required or permitted to be given under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be delivered personally, by certified mail return receipt requested, by overnight courier service, or by email with confirmation of receipt, addressed to the party at the address set forth below or such other address as a party may designate from time to time:

If to Company:
Meridian Mechanical of Illinois, LLC
Chief Operating Officer
1455 Busse Road
Elk Grove Village, Illinois 60007

If to Employee:
Hector Bancroft
[Address on File]

13. GOVERNING LAW

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, without regard to its conflict of laws provisions. Employee and Company each consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in DuPage County, Illinois for the resolution of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement. Employee waives any objection to venue in such courts and any claim that such courts are an inconvenient forum.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Separation Agreement and General Release as of the date first written above.
